pride_data.title: Human OTX2 TurboID Analysis in Transfected HDMB03 Cells
pride_data.projectDescription: HDMB03 cells were transiently transfected with plasmids expressing NLS-TurboID or 3xHA-TurboID-OTX2 under the control of a strong CAG promoter. After a 15-minute pulse with 500 µM exogenous biotin, RIPA lysates were prepared and processed with streptavin-sepharose to capture biotinylated proteins that were identified by using mass spectrometry.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Transfected HDMB03 umorspheres were washed in PBS and lysed with 1 ml of 1 x RIPA [20 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5; 150 mM NaCl; 1 mM EDTA-Na2; 1 mM EGTA; 1% NP-40; 1% sodium deoxycholate; 2.5 mM sodium pyrophosphate; 1 mM β-glycerophosphate; 1 mM Na3VO4, 1X Halt™ Protease/Phosphatase inhibitor (Thermo Scientific™)] for 10 minutes. Samples were then sonicated over 2 x 10s pulses at 30% load to shear DNA (Fisher Scientific Sonicator FB50 with microprobe) and clarified by centrifugation at 16 000 x g for 10 minutes at 4°C. Supernatants were quantified using the Bradford protein assay. Streptavidin-sepharose bead slurries (50 µl aliquots) were washed once in 1 ml of 1X RIPA. Washed beads were resuspended in 1 ml of 1X RIPA containing 2 mg of protein supernatant and rotated at 4°C overnight. The next day, samples were centrifuged for 5 minutes at 1000 x g, and bead pellets were washed twice in 1 ml 2% SDS solution (in ddH2O) and then three times (8 min each time) in 1 ml Wash Buffer (50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.4, 8 M Urea), at room temperature. Samples were resuspended in Storage Buffer (285 μl of ammonium bicarbonate (50 mM) and 15 μl of 1 mM biotin) and stored on ice.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: An Orbitrap Exploris 480 instrument (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Bremen, Germany) was used to obtain MS data as described in Hendrikse et al.  Nature 609, 1021-1028 (2022). Briefly, all MS raw files were processed with Proteome Discoverer (v2.20.388) at the Manitoba Centre for Proteomics and Systems Biology  and searched for tryptic peptides against the human Uniprot protein database (Dec, 2020) using SEQUEST with standard Orbitrap settings previously described and as follows: up to 2 missed cleavages were permitted, with a parent and fragment mass tolerance of 0.02 Da and 15 ppm. A fixed modification of cysteine carbamidomethylation was applied, and variable modifications including deamidation (at N and Q), N-terminal acetylation, oxidation (at M and W), phosphorylation (at S, T and Y), ubiquitylation (at K), double oxidation (at M and W) and biotinylation (at K) were permitted. Results were filtered by 1% False discovery rates (FDRs) at both the peptide and protein levels. SAINTexpress (v1.0.0) was used to calculate the probability of each potential proximal protein interaction from background contaminants using default parameters (N=4 OTX2 biological replicates and N=3 control biological replicates).
